source.title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning

accepted.question_text: For the k-nearest-neighbor decision rule, how fast does the probability of error Pe[k-NN] converge to the Bayes error Pe as the training-set size n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: How fast does the error rate Pe[k-NN] approach the Bayes error Pe as n approaches infinity, and what is the finite-sample performance of the k-NN-rule

accepted.question_text: What is the finite-sample performance of the k-nearest-neighbor decision rule when the training set is finite rather than infinite?

evidence.quote: How fast does the error rate Pe[k-NN] approach the Bayes error Pe as n approaches infinity, and what is the finite-sample performance of the k-NN-rule

accepted.question_text: How can the storage required for the training set in an instance-based learning system be reduced without degrading the performance of the resulting decision rule?

evidence.quote: How can the storage of the training set be reduced without degrading the performance of the decision rule?

accepted.question_text: How should a reduced training set be selected so that it still represents the different classes well enough for effective instance-based classification?

evidence.quote: How should the reduced training set be selected to represent the different classes?

accepted.question_text: How large should the neighborhood size k be in the k-nearest-neighbor rule, and how should that value of k be chosen from the data?

evidence.quote: How large should k be? How should a value of k be chosen?

accepted.question_text: In the k-nearest-neighbor rule, should all k neighbors contribute equally to the classification of an unknown pattern, or should they be weighted differently, and if so how should those neighbor weights be chosen?

evidence.quote: Should all k neighbors be equally weighted when used to decide the class of an unknown pattern? If not, how should the weights be chosen?

accepted.question_text: Should all measured features or attributes be weighted equally in an instance-based learning rule, and if not, how should the feature weights be selected?

evidence.quote: Should all the features (attributes) we weighted equally and if not how should the feature weights be chosen?

accepted.question_text: Which distance metric should be used when determining nearest neighbors in instance-based learning?

evidence.quote: Which distance metric should be used?

accepted.question_text: How can a nearest-neighbor decision rule be made robust when the training data contain overlapping classes or noise?

evidence.quote: How can the rule be made robust to overlapping classes or noise present in the training data?

accepted.question_text: How can a nearest-neighbor decision rule be made invariant to scaling of the measurements?

evidence.quote: How can the rule be made invariant to scaling of the measurements?

accepted.question_text: How can the nearest neighbors of a new query point be computed efficiently?

evidence.quote: How can the nearest neighbors of a new point be computed efficiently?

accepted.question_text: What is the smallest neural network that can implement nearest-neighbor decision rules?

evidence.quote: What is the smallest neural network that can implement nearest neighbor decision rules?

accepted.question_text: Let {X, Y} be a training set of n labeled patterns in d dimensions, and let C be the condensed training-set-consistent subset produced by Hart's condensed nearest neighbor rule. A naive brute-force algorithm computes C in O(dn^3) time. By how much can the complexity of computing this condensed subset be reduced?

evidence.quote: using a naive brute-force algorithm the complexity of computing the condensed subset of {X, Y } is O(dn3). In practice no efforts have been made to use other than brute-force algorithms. It is an open problem to determine how much this complexity can be reduced.

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of computing the reduced training-set-consistent subset produced by Gates' reduced nearest neighbor rule after CNN post-processing?

evidence.quote: The complexity of computing such a reduced consistent subset is an open problem.

accepted.question_text: The selective nearest neighbor rule SNN is reported empirically to have average running time O(dn^3). Can one prove theoretical results giving average-case running-time bounds of this kind for SNN?

evidence.quote: Wilson and Martinez [41] and Wilson [42] claim that the average running time of SNN is O(dn3). No theoretical results along these lines are known.

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of finding the smallest-size training-set-consistent subset when the classification problem has exactly two classes?

evidence.quote: Wilfong [40] showed in 1991 that the problem of finding the smallest size training-set consistent subset is NP-complete when there are three or more classes. The complexity for the case of two classes remains open.

accepted.question_text: In high-dimensional data, can one design worst-case algorithms for computing the Gabriel graph or the rectangular-influence graph of a training set {X, Y} in o(dn^3) time?

evidence.quote: Finding algorithms for computing these graphs in o(dn3) worst-case time is an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Fix a proximity graph such as the relative neighborhood graph or Gabriel graph on a labeled training set {X, Y} in d dimensions. Given an unknown query point Z to classify, how can one answer quickly which elements of {X, Y} are graph neighbors of Z?

evidence.quote: for any particular graph (relative neigh￾bor, Gabriel, etc.) and a training set {X, Y }, in order to classify an unknown Z we would like to be able to answer quickly the query: which elements of {X, Y } are the graph neighbors of Z?

accepted.question_text: Can the graph neighbors of a query point be computed approximately rather than exactly, while guaranteeing that the resulting approximation does not adversely affect classification error?

evidence.quote: Another fertile area which has not been investigated concerns the efficient computation of the graph neighbors of a query point, approximately, rather than exactly, with the constraint that the error in classification not be adversely affected.

accepted.question_text: Can one design efficient algorithms for inserting and deleting vertices in useful proximity graphs such as the Gabriel graph, the relative-neighborhood graph, and the rectangular-influence graph, so that rotation-based or related error-estimation procedures can be carried out efficiently?

evidence.quote: Hence it would be desirable to have efficient algorithms for in￾serting and deleting vertices from the most useful proximity graphs such as the Gabriel graph, the relative-neighborhood graph and the rectangular-influence graph.

accepted.question_text: Is there a condensing algorithm for instance-based learning that works well both when the data distributions are homogeneous and when they are not, rather than performing well in only one of those situations?

evidence.quote: Therefore a challenging open problem is to find an algorithm that works well in all situations.

Extracted the introductory open-question cluster on asymptotics, finite-sample behavior, storage reduction, subset selection, k selection, weighting, metric choice, robustness, scaling, search efficiency, and neural-network size.
Extracted explicit open complexity questions for Hart's CNN condensed subset and Gates' RNN reduced subset.
Extracted the missing theoretical average-case analysis for SNN and the open two-class complexity question for minimum consistent subsets.
Extracted the explicit open problem on worst-case high-dimensional construction of Gabriel and rectangular-influence graphs.
Extracted algorithmic query problems for exact and approximate graph-neighbor computation for a query point Z.
Extracted open problems on dynamic graph updates for error estimation and on a condensing algorithm that performs well across heterogeneous and homogeneous data distributions.
Rewrote each extracted item into standalone form by inlining the ambient setting when needed, especially for CNN, RNN, SNN, and graph-neighbor query questions.
Kept the introductory question cluster split into distinct canonical items because each asks about a different design or theory problem; no near-duplicates required merging.
Accepted items are self-contained, backed by verbatim source quotes with PDF page numbers, and do not rely on metadata-only evidence or unresolved cross-references.
